sanskrit: pratipraviṣṭe laṅkāṃ tu kṛtārthe rāvaṇātmaje rāghavaṃ parivāryārtā rarakṣur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: When the son of Rāvaṇa had re-entered Laṅkā, his mission accomplished, the foremost of the monkeys stood guard around Rāghava, anxious on his behalf.

sanskrit: hanūmān aṅgado nīlaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kumudo nalaḥ gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
english: Hanūmān, Aṅgada, Nīla, Suṣeṇa, Kumuda, Nala, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, and Gandhamādana —

sanskrit: jāmbavān ṛṣabhaḥ sundo rambhaḥ śatabaliḥ pṛthuḥ vyūḍhānīkāś ca yattāś ca drumān ādāya sarvataḥ
english: Jāmbavān, Ṛṣabha, Sunda, Rambha, Śatabali, and Pṛthu — all standing in battle array, alert, taking up trees on every side,

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇā diśaḥ sarvās tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca vānarāḥ tṛṇeṣv api ca ceṣṭatsu rākṣasā iti menire
english: the monkeys scanned all directions, crosswise and above, and even when blades of grass stirred they thought it was a rākṣasa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaś cāpi saṃhṛṣṭo visṛjyendrajitaṃ sutam ājuhāva tataḥ sītā rakṣaṇī rākṣasīs tadā
english: Rāvaṇa too, greatly pleased, having dismissed his son Indrajit, then summoned the rākṣasī women who guarded Sītā.

sanskrit: rākṣasyas trijaṭā cāpi śāsanāt tam upasthitāḥ tā uvāca tato hṛṣṭo rākṣasī rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: The rākṣasīs along with Trijaṭā appeared before him at his command. Then the lord of the rākṣasas, overjoyed, addressed those rākṣasī women.

sanskrit: hatāv indrajitākhyāta vaidehyā rāmalakṣmaṇau puṣpakaṃ ca samāropya darśayadhvaṃ hatau raṇe
english: "Announce to the daughter of Videha that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa have been slain by Indrajit. Mount her on Puṣpaka and show her the two slain in battle."

sanskrit: yad āśrayād avaṣṭabdho neyaṃ mām upatiṣṭhati so 'syā bhartā saha bhrātrā nirasto raṇamūrdhani
english: "He who was her refuge and on whom she relied, the one for whose sake she would not come to me — that husband of hers, together with his brother, has been cast down on the battlefield."

sanskrit: nirviśaṅkā nirudvignā nirapekṣā ca maithilī mām upasthāsyate sītā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
english: "Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, free from doubt, free from distress, freed of all expectations, adorned with every ornament, will come to attend upon me."

sanskrit: adya kālavaśaṃ prāptaṃ raṇe rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam avekṣya vinivṛttāśā nānyāṃ gatim apaśyatī
english: "Having seen Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, come under the sway of death on the battlefield today, with her hope extinguished and seeing no other recourse, she will turn to me."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ rākṣasyas tās tathety uktvā prajagmur yatra puṣpakam
english: Hearing those words of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, those rākṣasī women replied "So be it" and went to where Puṣpaka stood.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣpakam ādaya rākṣasyo rāvaṇājñayā aśokavanikāsthāṃ tāṃ maithilīṃ samupānayan
english: Then the rākṣasīs, taking Puṣpaka by Rāvaṇa's command, brought the princess of Mithilā who was in the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: tām ādāya tu rākṣasyo bhartṛśokaparāyaṇām sītām āropayām āsur vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tadā
english: Taking her — Sītā, utterly absorbed in grief for her husband — the rākṣasīs had her ascend the aerial vehicle Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣpakam āropya sītāṃ trijaṭayā saha rāvaṇo 'kārayal laṅkāṃ patākādhvajamālinīm
english: Then, having placed Sītā together with Trijaṭā on Puṣpaka, Rāvaṇa had Laṅkā decorated with garlands of banners and flags.

sanskrit: prāghoṣayata hṛṣṭaś ca laṅkāyāṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ rāghavo lakṣmaṇaś caiva hatāv indrajitā raṇe
english: And the lord of the rākṣasas, filled with joy, proclaimed throughout Laṅkā: "Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa have been slain in battle by Indrajit."

sanskrit: vimānenāpi sītā tu gatvā trijaṭayā saha dadarśa vānarāṇāṃ tu sarvaṃ sinyaṃ nipātitam
english: And Sītā, traveling by that aerial vehicle with Trijaṭā, saw the entire monkey army laid low.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanasaś cāpi dadarśa piśitāśanān vānarāṃś cāpi duḥkhārtān rāmalakṣmaṇapārśvataḥ
english: She saw the flesh-eating rākṣasas exulting in their minds, and the monkeys stricken with grief by the side of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ sītā dadarśobhau śayānau śatatalpayoḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva rāmaṃ ca visaṃjñau śarapīḍitau
english: Then Sītā beheld them both lying on their beds of arrows — Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma — unconscious, tormented by shafts.

sanskrit: vidhvastakavacau vīrau vipraviddhaśarāsanau sāyakaiś chinnasarvāṅgau śarastambhamayau kṣitau
english: The two heroes, their armor shattered, their bows flung apart, every limb of their bodies cut by arrows, lay on the ground like pillars fashioned of arrows.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau tatra vīrau sā puruṣarṣabhau duḥkhārtā subhṛśaṃ sītā karuṇaṃ vilalāpa ha
english: Seeing those two brothers there, those two bull-like men, Sītā, deeply afflicted with grief, lamented piteously.

sanskrit: sā bāṣpaśokābhihatā samīkṣya tau bhrātarau devasamaprabhāvau vitarkayantī nidhanaṃ tayoḥ sā duḥkhānvitā vākyam idaṃ jagāda
english: She, struck by tears and sorrow, gazing at those two brothers equal in splendor to gods, contemplating their death, overcome with grief, spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ sītā karuṇaṃ śokakarśitā
english: Seeing her husband slain and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā lamented piercingly and piteously, worn down by grief.

sanskrit: ūcur lakṣaṇikā ye māṃ putriṇy avidhaveti ca te 'sya sarve hate rāme 'jñānino 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: "Those who read auspicious marks who said to me, 'You shall have sons, you shall not be widowed' — all of them, now that Rāma is slain, were ignorant and spoke falsehood."

sanskrit: yajvano mahiṣīṃ ye mām ūcuḥ patnīṃ ca satriṇaḥ te 'dya sarve hate rāme 'jñānino 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: "Those who perform sacrifices who called me the chief queen, and those who perform soma rites who called me their patron's wife — all of them now that Rāma is slain were ignorant and spoke falsehood."

sanskrit: vīrapārthivapatnī tvaṃ ye dhanyeti ca māṃ viduḥ te 'dya sarve hate rāme 'jñānino 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: "Those who knew me as 'wife of a heroic king' and called me fortunate — all of them now that Rāma is slain were ignorant and spoke falsehood."

sanskrit: ūcuḥ saṃśravaṇe ye māṃ dvijāḥ kārtāntikāḥ śubhām te 'dya sarve hate rāme 'jñānino 'nṛtavādinaḥ
english: "Those twice-born readers of fate who declared me auspicious when I was presented — all of them now that Rāma is slain were ignorant and spoke falsehood."

sanskrit: imāni khalu padmāni pādayor yaiḥ kila striyaḥ adhirājye 'bhiṣicyante narendraiḥ patibhiḥ saha
english: "Indeed these lotus marks on the feet, by which women are said to be consecrated to sovereignty alongside their husbands, kings of men —

sanskrit: vaidhavyaṃ yānti yair nāryo 'lakṣaṇair bhāgyadurlabhāḥ nātmanas tāni paśyāmi paśyantī hatalakṣaṇā
english: "and those ill-omened marks by which women become widows, unfortunate and deprived of good fortune — seeing as I am one whose auspicious signs have been destroyed, I do not see those in myself."

sanskrit: satyānīmāni padmāni strīṇām uktvāni lakṣaṇe tāny adya nihate rāme vitathāni bhavanti me
english: "These lotus marks declared true for women according to physiognomy — they become meaningless for me today, now that Rāma is slain."

sanskrit: keśāḥ sūkṣmāḥ samā nīlā bhruvau cāsaṃgate mama vṛtte cālomaśe jaṅghe dantāś cāviralā mama
english: "My hair is fine, even, and dark; my eyebrows are not joined; my calves are rounded and hairless; my teeth are without gaps."

sanskrit: śaṅkhe netre karau pādau gulphāv ūrū ca me citau anuvṛttā nakhāḥ snigdhāḥ samāś cāṅgulayo mama
english: "My temples, eyes, hands, feet, and ankles are well-formed; my thighs are full; my nails are curved, smooth, and even; my fingers are well-proportioned."

sanskrit: stanau cāviralau pīnau mamemau magnacūcukau magnā cotsaṅginī nābhiḥ pārśvoraskaṃ ca me citam
english: "My two breasts are close-set and full with sunken nipples; my navel is deep and set high; and my flanks and chest are well-formed."

sanskrit: mama varṇo maṇinibho mṛdūny aṅgaruhāṇi ca pratiṣṭhitāṃ dvadaśabhir mām ūcuḥ śubhalakṣaṇām
english: "My complexion is like a jewel, and my body hair is fine. Those who read twelve signs declared me established in auspicious marks."

sanskrit: samagrayavam acchidraṃ pāṇipādaṃ ca varṇavat mandasmitety eva ca māṃ kanyālakṣaṇikā viduḥ
english: "My palms and soles, with unbroken barleycorn lines and beautiful in color, and my gentle smile — by these the readers of maidens' marks recognized me."

sanskrit: adhirājye 'bhiṣeko me brāhmaṇaiḥ patinā saha kṛtāntakuśalair uktaṃ tat sarvaṃ vitathīkṛtam
english: "A consecration to sovereignty alongside my husband — what was declared by those brāhmaṇas skilled in the knowledge of fate, all of that has been made false."

sanskrit: śodhayitvā janasthānaṃ pravṛttim upalabhya ca tīrtvā sāgaram akṣobhyaṃ bhrātarau goṣpade hatau
english: "After clearing out Janasthāna, after obtaining news of me, after crossing the unfordable ocean — the two brothers have been slain as if in a puddle of water."

sanskrit: nanu vāruṇam āgneyam aindraṃ vāyavyam eva ca astraṃ brahmaśiraś caiva rāghavau pratyapadyatām
english: "Did not the two Rāghavas indeed command the water-weapon, the fire-weapon, the Indra-weapon, the wind-weapon, and the Brahmaśiras missile as well?"

sanskrit: adṛśyamānena raṇe māyayā vāsavopamau mama nāthāv anāthāyā nihatau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "By means of illusion, by one unseen in battle, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa — the two lords equal to Vāsava, my protectors though I am without protection — have been slain."

sanskrit: na hi dṛṣṭipathaṃ prāpya rāghavasya raṇe ripuḥ jīvan pratinivarteta yady api syān manojavaḥ
english: "For no enemy, once he came within the field of vision of Rāghava in battle, could return alive, even if he were swift as thought."

sanskrit: na kālasyātibhāro 'sti kṛtāntaś ca sudurjayaḥ yatra rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā śete yudhi nipāthitaḥ
english: "There is nothing too heavy for Time; Fate is utterly unconquerable — for here lies Rāma together with his brother, struck down in battle."

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śocāmi bhartāraṃ nihataṃ na ca lakṣmaṇam nātmānaṃ jananī cāpi yathā śvaśrūṃ tapasvinīm
english: "I do not grieve so much for my slain husband, nor for Lakṣmaṇa, nor for myself, as I do for my mother-in-law, that ascetic woman."

sanskrit: sā hi cintayate nityaṃ samāptavratam āgatam kadā drakṣyāmi sītāṃ ca rāmaṃ ca sahalakṣmaṇam
english: "For she thinks constantly, 'When shall I see one whose vow is fulfilled and returned — when shall I see Sītā and Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa?'"

sanskrit: paridevayamānāṃ tāṃ rākṣasī trijaṭābravīt mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā devi bhartāyaṃ tava jīvati
english: As she lamented thus, the rākṣasī Trijaṭā spoke to her: "Do not despair, my lady — your husband is alive."

sanskrit: kāraṇāni ca vakṣyāmi mahānti sadṛśāni ca yathemau jīvato devi bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "And I shall tell you the great and fitting reasons why these two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are alive, my lady."

sanskrit: na hi kopaparītāni harṣaparyutsukāni ca bhavanti yudhi yodhānāṃ mukhāni nihate patau
english: "For the faces of warriors in battle do not become flooded with anger and quivering with joy when their master has been slain."

sanskrit: idaṃ vimānaṃ vaidehi puṣpakaṃ nāma nāmataḥ divyaṃ tvāṃ dhārayen nedaṃ yady etau gajajīvitau
english: "This divine aerial vehicle, called Puṣpaka by name, O daughter of Videha, would not bear you if these two were as dead as elephants slain."

sanskrit: hatavīrapradhānā hi hatotsāhā nirudyamā senā bhramati saṃkhyeṣu hatakarṇeva naur jale
english: "An army whose foremost heroes have been slain, with its energy destroyed and its effort collapsed, wanders about in battle like a rudderless ship on water."

sanskrit: iyaṃ punar asaṃbhrāntā nirudvignā tarasvinī senā rakṣati kākutsthau māyayā nirjitau raṇe
english: "This army, on the other hand, unperturbed and undistressed, full of energy, protects the two Kākutsthas who have been overcome by illusion in battle."

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ bhava suvisrabdhā anumānaiḥ sukhodayaiḥ ahatau paśya kākutsthau snehād etad bravīmi te
english: "Therefore be completely reassured. By these signs from which good will arise, see that the two Kākutsthas are not slain. I tell you this out of affection."

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadā cana cāritrasukhaśīlatvāt praviṣṭāsi mano mama
english: "I have never spoken falsehood before, nor shall I ever speak it. Because of the pleasure I take in good conduct, you have entered my heart."

sanskrit: nemau śakyau raṇe jetuṃ sendrair api surāsuraiḥ etayor ānanaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā cāveditaṃ tava
english: "These two cannot be conquered in battle even by the gods and asuras together with Indra. Having seen their faces, I have reported this to you."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca sumahac cihnaṃ śanaiḥ paśyasva maithili niḥsaṃjñāv apy ubhāv etau naiva lakṣmīr viyujyate
english: "And observe this very great sign, O princess of Mithilā: though both of them are unconscious, their radiance does not depart from them."

sanskrit: prāyeṇa gatasattvānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ gatāyuṣām dṛśyamāneṣu vaktreṣu paraṃ bhavati vaikṛtam
english: "In general, in the faces of men who have lost their vital force and whose life has departed, a great change becomes visible."

sanskrit: tyaja śokaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca mohaṃ ca janakātmaje rāmalakṣmaṇayor arthe nādya śakyam ajīvitum
english: "Abandon grief and pain and delusion, O daughter of Janaka. For the sake of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa it is not possible to cease living today."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasyāḥ sītā surasutopamā kṛtāñjalir uvācedam evam astv iti maithilī
english: Hearing those words of hers, Sītā, equal to the daughter of a god, joined her palms and said: "Let it be so" — the princess of Mithilā.

sanskrit: vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ tat tu samivartya manojavam dīnā trijaṭayā sītā laṅkām eva praveśitā
english: Then that swift Puṣpaka aerial vehicle was turned about, and Sītā, forlorn, was conducted back into Laṅkā itself by Trijaṭā.

sanskrit: tatas trijaṭayā sārdhaṃ puṣpakād avaruhya sā aśokavanikām eva rakṣasībhiḥ praveśitā
english: Then, having descended from Puṣpaka together with Trijaṭā, she was conducted by the rākṣasī women back into the Aśoka grove itself.

sanskrit: praviśya sītā bahuvṛkṣaṣaṇḍāṃ tāṃ rākṣasendrasya vihārabhūmim saṃprekṣya saṃcintya ca rājaputrau paraṃ viṣādaṃ samupājagāma
english: Entering that pleasure-ground of the lord of the rākṣasas dense with many groves of trees, and gazing upon and reflecting on the two princes, Sītā fell into the deepest despair.

sanskrit: ghoreṇa śarabandhena baddhau daśarathātmajau niśvasantau yathā nāgau śayānau rudhirokṣitau
english: The two sons of Daśaratha, bound by a dreadful net of arrows, lay breathing like great serpents, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: sarve te vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ sasugrīvā mahābalāḥ parivārya mahātmānau tasthuḥ śokapariplutāḥ
english: All those foremost of the monkeys, the mighty ones with Sugrīva, stood surrounding the two great-souled princes, overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rāmaḥ pratyabudhyata vīryavān sthiratvāt sattvayogāc ca śaraiḥ saṃdānito 'pi san
english: In the meantime, the valiant Rāma regained consciousness, even though bound by arrows, through steadiness and the force of his vital spirit.

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvā sarudhiraṃ viṣaṇṇaṃ gāḍham arpitam bhrātaraṃ dīnavadanaṃ paryadevayad āturaḥ
english: Then, seeing his brother — covered in blood, deeply afflicted, pierced through, his face downcast — he lamented, overcome with anguish.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me sītayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ jīvitena vā śayānaṃ yo 'dya paśyāmi bhrātaraṃ yudhi nirjitam
english: "What need have I of Sītā, what need of life itself, I who now see my brother lying overcome in battle?"

sanskrit: śakyā sītā samā nārī prāptuṃ loke vicinvatā na lakṣmaṇasamo bhrātā sacivaḥ sāmparāyikaḥ
english: "A woman equal to Sītā can be found by searching in the world. A brother equal to Lakṣmaṇa, a counselor and companion in war, cannot."

sanskrit: parityakṣyāmy ahaṃ prāṇān vānarāṇāṃ tu paśyatām yadi pañcatvam āpannaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ
english: "I shall abandon my life before the eyes of the monkeys, if Sumitrā's joy-increasing son has attained the five elements."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi kausalyāṃ mātaraṃ kiṃ nu kaikayīm katham ambāṃ sumitrāṃca putradarśanalālasām
english: "What shall I say to Kausalyā my mother? What to Kaikeyī? How shall I console mother Sumitrā, who longs to see her son?"

sanskrit: vivatsāṃ vepamānāṃ ca krośantīṃ kurarīm iva katham āśvāsayiṣyāmi yadi yāsyāmi taṃ vinā
english: "How shall I comfort her, bereft of her child, trembling and crying out like an osprey, if I go back without him?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ vakṣyāmi śatrughnaṃ bharataṃ ca yaśasvinam mayā saha vanaṃ yāto vinā tenāgataḥ punaḥ
english: "How shall I speak to Śatrughna and the illustrious Bharata? He went to the forest with me, and I have returned without him."

sanskrit: upālambhaṃ na śakṣyāmi soḍhuṃ bata sumitrayā ihaiva dehaṃ tyakṣyāmi na hi jīvitum utsahe
english: "Alas, I shall not be able to bear Sumitrā's reproach. I shall abandon my body here; I have no desire to live."

sanskrit: dhiṅ māṃ duṣkṛtakarmāṇam anāryaṃ yatkṛte hy asau lakṣmaṇaḥ patitaḥ śete śaratalpe gatāsuvat
english: "Shame on me, a doer of evil deeds, ignoble — for whose sake this Lakṣmaṇa has fallen and lies on his bed of arrows, as if his life has departed."

sanskrit: tvaṃ nityaṃ suviṣaṇṇaṃ mām āśvāsayasi lakṣmaṇa gatāsur nādya śaknoṣi mām ārtam abhibhāṣitum
english: "You, Lakṣmaṇa, always used to console me when I was deeply despondent. Now, your life gone, you are not able today to address me in my anguish."

sanskrit: yenādya bahavo yuddhe rākṣasā nihatāḥ kṣitau tasyām eva kṣitau vīraḥ sa śete nihataḥ paraiḥ
english: "By whom many rākṣasas were struck down to the earth in battle today — on that same earth the hero himself lies, struck down by his enemies."

sanskrit: śayānaḥ śaratalpe 'smin svaśoṇitapariplutaḥ śarajālaiś cito bhāti bhāskaro 'stam iva vrajan
english: "Lying on this bed of arrows, drenched in his own blood, covered with a web of arrows, he shines like the sun going to its setting."

sanskrit: bāṇābhihatamarmatvān na śaknoty abhivīkṣitum rujā cābruvato hy asya dṛṣṭirāgeṇa sūcyate
english: "Because his vital spots are struck by arrows, he cannot look up; and though he speaks no word of his pain, it is indicated by the redness of his gaze."

sanskrit: yathaiva māṃ vanaṃ yāntam anuyāto mahādyutiḥ aham apy anuyāsyāmi tathaivainaṃ yamakṣayam
english: "Just as this great-splendored one followed me when I went to the forest, so too shall I follow him to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: iṣṭabandhujano nityaṃ māṃ ca nityam anuvrataḥ imām adya gato 'vasthāṃ mamānāryasya durnayaiḥ
english: "A dear kinsman, ever devoted to me and ever in attendance on me — he has come to this condition today through the wicked conduct of an ignoble one like me."

sanskrit: suruṣṭenāpi vīreṇa lakṣmaṇenā na saṃsmare paruṣaṃ vipriyaṃ vāpi śrāvitaṃ na kadā cana
english: "Even when provoked, the hero Lakṣmaṇa — I do not recall that he ever caused me to hear a harsh or displeasing word."

sanskrit: visasarjaikavegena pañcabāṇaśatāni yaḥ iṣvastreṣv adhikas tasmāt kārtavīryāc ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "He who could release five hundred arrows in a single surge, surpassing Kārtavīrya himself in the science of archery — that is Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi yo hanyāc chakrasyāpi mahātmanaḥ so 'yam urvyāṃhataḥ śete mahārhaśayanocitaḥ
english: "He who could counter weapons with weapons even against the great-souled Śakra — that same man now lies struck down on the earth, though fit for the most honored bed."

sanskrit: tac ca mithyā pralaptaṃ māṃ pradhakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ yan mayā na kṛto rājā rākṣasānāṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: "And that false boast will surely consume me — that I did not make Vibhīṣaṇa king of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: asmin muhūrte sugrīva pratiyātum ito 'rhasi matvā hīnaṃ mayā rājan rākṣaso 'bhidraved balī
english: "At this very moment, Sugrīva, you ought to depart from here. The mighty lord of the rākṣasas may attack, considering me to be diminished."

sanskrit: aṅgadaṃ tu puraskṛtya sasainyaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ sāgaraṃ tara sugrīva punas tenaiva setunā
english: "Placing Aṅgada at the fore, together with your army and your allies, Sugrīva, cross the ocean again by that same bridge."

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ hanumatā kāryaṃ yad anyair duṣkaraṃ raṇe ṛkṣarājena tuṣyāmi golāṅgūlādhipena ca
english: "The deed accomplished by Hanūmān was one difficult for others in battle. I am satisfied with the king of the bears and with the lord of the golāṅgūla monkeys."

sanskrit: aṅgadena kṛtaṃ karma maindena dvividena ca yuddhaṃ kesariṇā saṃkhye ghoraṃ saṃpātinā kṛtam
english: "The deed done by Aṅgada, and by Mainda and Dvivida, and the terrible battle fought in the conflict by Kesarin and Saṃpāti —"

sanskrit: gavayena gavākṣeṇa śarabheṇa gajena ca anyaiś ca haribhir yuddhaṃ madārthe tyaktajīvitaiḥ
english: "and the battle of Gavaya, Gavākṣa, Śarabha, Gaja, and other monkeys who abandoned their lives for my sake —"

sanskrit: na cātikramituṃ śakyaṃ daivaṃ sugrīva mānuṣaiḥ yat tu śakyaṃ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṃtapa kṛtaṃ sugrīva tat sarvaṃ bhavatādharmabhīruṇā
english: "Fate cannot be overcome by human beings, O Sugrīva. But whatever was possible for a friend and companion to do, all of that, O scorcher of foes, has been done by you, who fear adharma."

sanskrit: mitrakāryaṃ kṛtam idaṃ bhavadbhir vānararṣabhāḥ anujñātā mayā sarve yatheṣṭaṃ gantum arhatha
english: "This duty of friendship has been done by all of you, O foremost of monkeys. Dismissed by me, you are all free to go wherever you wish."

sanskrit: śuśruvus tasya te sarve vānarāḥ paridevitam vartayāṃ cakrur aśrūṇi netraiḥ kṛṣṇetarekṣaṇāḥ
english: All those monkeys heard his lament and let tears flow from their eyes, whose whites were darker than dark.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇy anīkāni sthāpayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ ājagāma gadāpāṇis tvarito yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, having stationed all the troops, came swiftly with mace in hand to where Rāghava was.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tvaritaṃ yāntaṃ nīlāñjanacayopamam vānarā dudruvuḥ sarve manyamānās tu rāvaṇim
english: Seeing him advancing swiftly, dark as a mass of blue collyrium, all the monkeys fled, thinking him to be Rāvaṇa's son.
